policies.title: United States ordinary passports: specified visa-free short visits
policies.summary: Current State Department entry guidance establishes visa-free visitor access for the listed destination-specific ordinary U.S. passport scopes.
conditions: Visitor/tourism scope only; work, residence, transit, special-document, dual-nationality and final-admission rules remain outside this classification.
TN: up to 90 days; UA: up to 90 days in 180, with health-insurance and funds requirements; VG: 30 days or less; PA: 180 days; BA: 90 days in six months.
For UA, visa status does not establish border accessibility or override martial-law, carrier, registration, document and security conditions.

policies.title: United States ordinary passports: explicitly pre-travel electronic visas
policies.summary: Current State Department guidance explicitly requires electronic visa approval before arrival for the listed destinations.
conditions: IQ: obtain an e-Visa through the Iraq e-Visa Portal before arrival; distinct KRG entry alternatives do not widen this nationwide classification.
GQ: complete the e-visa application, receive approval before arrival, and carry the printed approval.
Visitor purpose, passport validity, entry-point, special-document and final-admission conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: United States ordinary passports: expressly available arrival visas
policies.summary: Current State Department guidance expressly describes an arrival-issuance route for the listed destinations, subject to each stated limitation.
conditions: SY: tourist visa may be issued on arrival at Damascus International Airport or at land entry from Lebanon or Jordan; 30-day stay, fee and Israeli-document restrictions apply.
DJ: visitors may apply on arrival; the stated fee is USD 23.
KM: visa is available on arrival and payment is in cash USD or euros.
TM: obtain the required letter of invitation first; then an airport visa route is available at Ashgabat. Registration, purpose, document and final-admission conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: United States ordinary passports: expressly pre-travel visas
policies.summary: Current State Department guidance expressly requires a visa to be obtained before travel for the listed destinations.
conditions: LY: applications are made at the Libyan embassy in the applicant's country of residence, require MFA approval, and visas are unavailable at the port of entry.
SD: obtain the visa from a Sudanese embassy before arrival; SS and CF: obtain the visa before arrival/travel.
CG: obtain the visa before travel; invitation or hotel-reservation conditions apply.
Visitor purpose, passport validity, invitation, transit, special-document and final-admission conditions remain applicable.

conflicts.explanation: State guidance requires embassy issuance after MFA approval and says visas are unavailable at the port of entry; it does not establish electronic issuance.
State guidance expressly describes a tourist-visa-on-arrival route at specified Syrian entry points, not electronic issuance.
State guidance says a visa must be applied for and obtained before arrival and does not establish electronic issuance.
After a pre-travel letter of invitation, State guidance expressly permits applying for the visa at Ashgabat airport on arrival.

unresolved.reason: State guidance says a valid Afghan visa is needed but does not establish a current issuance route or timing; generic visa wording cannot be normalized under this batch's strict taxonomy.
A U.S. passport is invalid for travel absent a narrowly granted special validation. The taxonomy has no passport-invalid or entry-prohibited status.
State guidance makes access dependent on Israeli-controlled routes and Palestinian Authority population-registration or residence facts, not a clean ordinary U.S.-passport visitor classification.

U.S. law restricts Cuba travel activities and the reviewed official material does not provide a current U.S.-passport-only Cuban issuance route; the taxonomy has no equivalent outbound legal-restriction status.
State guidance reports Gabon's suspension of visa issuance to U.S. citizens. The taxonomy has no current visa-issuance-suspended or entry-prohibited status.
